thread:
jess_support: FYI customer (acct: acme-inc) opened an escalation — p99 latency spike for streaming responses. They say first chunk often comes late (~2.2s) but total completion time is normal. They included a short repro and logs.

sam_sre: can you paste the repro curl and which model/route they're hitting?

jess_support: sure — minimal repro they sent: 
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-infer","input":"long prompt to trigger streaming","stream":true}'
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They said behaviour is worse over our eu-west edge (~p99). Non-streaming requests don't show p99 spike.

maria_eng: hmm that's classic initial-chunk delay. A few possibilities: proxy coalescing at edge, h2 flow-control + server-side flush policy, or kernel-level Nagle on some mid-tier. Any deploys/rollouts?

jess_support: customer timestamped it starting around 2265429000 (about 8k seconds ago). No obvious deploy in their message. Can we check our recent rollouts?

deploybot: rollout service:canary -> stable at 2265427500 by maria_eng (model-serving runtime v5.3.2). No rollbacks.

sam_sre: ok timeline overlaps. Maria, did v5.3.2 change chunk buffering or default flush thresholds?

maria_eng: v5.3.2 includes an adaptive coalescing tweak: we increased min-chunk-interval to 30ms and introduced a small prefix-aggregation heuristic to reduce tiny payloads. Shouldn't add >1s delays but could interact badly with certain seq-length distributions.

jess_support: customer logs show repeated "first-chunk-delay" events with trace ids. They captured an HTTP/2 connection where first DATA frame arrives late. Attaching their snippet: 
```
[TRACE] trace_id=abc123 stage=edge-proxy wait=2150ms server-first-byte=18ms
```

tim_oncall: request-level traces show edge wait=~2s then server rtt small -> points to edge or upstream queuing. Can we run a quick A/B: flip streaming flush to force immediate flush on first token for a single customer? We have per-customer rollout flags.

maria_eng: yes we can. There's a flag streaming.immediate_first_chunk = true. I'll toggle for acme-inc in prod for 1h and monitor p99.

sam_sre: also ask customer to retry with HTTP/1.1 SSE path (Accept: text/event-stream + h1) to see if it's h2-specific. If h1 removes the 2s gap that suggests HTTP/2 coalescing/flow-control interaction.

jess_support: told them the plan, they prefer quick mitigation. Applied the flag at 2265431200 for acme-inc. I'll keep them in the loop.

maria_eng: added a short-term metric on first_byte_delay_by_customer and enabled 1-minute alerts for >1s p99. Instrumented at 2265431500.

tim_oncall: initial readouts: p99 for acme-inc dropped from ~2.1s -> 130ms after immediate_first_chunk toggle. That's a strong signal it's chunk-coalescing at our edge.

sam_sre: good. Next steps: 1) keep immediate_first_chunk for affected customers until we ship a safer runtime fix; 2) repro in staging with same edge config to root-cause; 3) consider reverting or tuning the min-chunk-interval heuristic in v5.3.2.

maria_eng: I can reproduce in staging by running a client that sends long prompt but with low initial token probability. Staging shows same ~2s initial gap when min-chunk-interval=30ms and the server buffers tiny prefix. Fix options: lower min-chunk-interval to 5ms or add explicit flush after prefix generation. I'll open a PR for a conservative fix (5ms + immediate-first-chunk opt-out).

jess_support: customer is happy with temporary toggle. They've asked for ETA for full fix. What timeline?

maria_eng: will push a patch to canary today (2265433500), verify across edge variants, then schedule stable rollout tomorrow if no regressions. ETA ~24h.

sam_sre: also note ops: add an edge rule to avoid TCP-level coalesce for SSE endpoints (disable Nagle for these routes) — ops team to evaluate.

tim_oncall: capturing tcpdump and h2 frames for the affected trace_ids to attach to the postmortem. Also tagging this incident for follow-up: incident#STREAM-226543.

jess_support: thanks everyone. I'll update the customer with the mitigation and ETA. Will circle back after canary validation. :thumbsup:

maria_eng: PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/8423 with change set + perf test.

jess_support: marking resolved for customer with workaround applied; keeping thread open for engineering follow-up.

sam_sre: leaving note: if we see other customers hitting this, we'll auto-apply immediate_first_chunk for orgs with p99>1s until full fix is rolled.

jess_support: noted. Closing loop later with postmortem and playbook entries for streaming regressions. :white_check_mark:
